subject: Surgery
title: Acute Pancreatitis: Diagnosis, Severity and Supportive Care
preview: Diagnose pancreatitis using compatible pain, pancreatic enzymes and/or imaging; management depends on severity and cause.

sections.title: Clinical pattern
points: Upper abdominal pain may radiate to the back, with nausea or vomiting.
Lipase is generally preferred over amylase in the diagnostic workup.

sections.title: Severity and complications
points: Evaluate organ dysfunction, hemodynamic status, respiratory function and complications rather than relying only on an older scoring system.
Address gallstone-related obstruction or infected complications according to clinical findings and specialist pathways.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A high enzyme concentration alone does not grade disease severity.
Prophylactic antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated sterile pancreatitis.

quickRevision: The diagnosis often relies on a typical clinical syndrome and elevated pancreatic enzymes, with imaging when needed.
Gallstones and alcohol are common causes; other etiologies include drugs and metabolic disorders.
Early treatment emphasizes analgesia, appropriate fluid assessment, nutrition and recognition of organ dysfunction.

quiz.question: Which biochemical test supports acute pancreatitis in appropriate clinical context?
quiz.explanation: Serum lipase. Lipase is generally preferred over amylase in the diagnostic workup.
